name: service
summary: Business-logic orchestrator that coordinates other components to accomplish one operation.
description: Creates a service class that encapsulates business logic and orchestrates collaborators
problem: You have a complex operation (process an order, settle a payout, sync an account) that spans multiple components — data access, events, notifications — and you need one platform-agnostic place that owns the workflow, applies the business rules, and handles failure consistently.
appliesWhen: An operation coordinates two or more components (datastores, strategies, other services)
Business rules need to be applied consistently in one place
The operation has failure states that need consistent error handling and logging
You want the 'doing' logic out of models, controllers, and listeners
Side effects should be broadcast as events rather than hard-coded calls
avoidWhen: The class would only convert data between formats — that's an adapter or factory
The class would only construct objects — that's a factory or builder
The class would only hold data — that's a model
The logic is a one-line delegation — call the collaborator directly
You're about to mix platform-specific calls into it — put those behind a strategy first
examples: I need somewhere to put the payout settlement workflow
Create a service that coordinates payment, inventory, and notification
Where should the refund business logic live
tradeoffs: One small file. Services with too many dependencies are hard to test — if the constructor grows past a handful of collaborators, split into smaller supporting services that compose.
outputs: A {name} service class with a constructor-injection seam for collaborators
postApply: Inject the collaborators this operation needs (datastores, strategies, other services)
Add public methods for the business operations, validating inputs early
Broadcast domain events for side effects instead of calling consumers directly
Throw domain-specific exceptions and log failures — keep error handling consistent
No DI registration is needed: the container resolves concrete classes automatically

name.aiHint: PascalCase, named for the operation it owns, ending in 'Service' (OrderProcessingService, RefundService). One service per type of business operation.
